headline: Crude's second leg down handed the market a disinflation gift and the market bought volatility with it — Brent -10.9%, breakevens cracked, and the front end still priced tighter.
summary: The oil unwind stopped being a dent and became a trend. Brent fell 10.9% to 104.83 and is -9.5% on the week; WTI -7.1% to 96.75, back under 100; RBOB gasoline -12.3% in a single session and -12.3% on the month (z=-1.22, rolling over), with US-Iran de-escalation headlines doing the work. The inflation leg finally transmitted: the 5-year breakeven broke 8bp on the week to 2.39 and the 10-year to 2.29, the 34th percentile of its year. Oil/gold fell 8.6% but is still +11.5% on the month and 26.1% above its 200-day — the risk-premium air is coming out fast, not finished.

Instead of a goldilocks bid, the market paid up for protection and for a hawkish Fed. VIX jumped 8.9% to 21.15, +38.1% on the month (z=1.49); VIX3M +3.9% to 21.60; the VIX/VIX3M term structure printed 0.979, +4.8% on the day at z=1.72 and turning up — near inversion. SKEW is 152.78. Yesterday vol refused to respond to a crude collapse; today it responded to the wrong thing. The curve says why: the 3-month bill rose 5bp to 4.21 (89th percentile) and the 2-year 3bp to 4.59 while the 10-year fell 3bp to 4.91 and the 30-year 3bp to 5.28. 2s10s flattened to 32bp (22nd percentile), 3m10y to 70bp, -39bp on the month. The 10-year real yield rose 2bp to 2.62 with breakevens falling — cheaper oil is being discounted as demand loss plus no cuts, not relief. Rates composite -32, credit & vol -27.

Beneath the 0.5% S&P decline sits a three-sigma rotation. RSP/SPY is +1.0% on the day and +5.9% on the month at z=3.00 with acceleration z=3.55, the most extreme reading on the board; equal-weight is +4.9% on the month at the 92nd percentile. This is not breadth as health, it is mega-cap de-risking: NDX -9.1% on the month against DJI +1.6%, QQQ/SPY at z=-2.37, SOXX -17.1%, SMH -14.2%, AMD -17.5%, MU -16.9%, ASML -13.5%, TSM -11.0%, GOOGL -18.7% (z=-2.50), META -15.2% (acceleration -2.62), XLC -10.0% and sitting at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. The money went straight into the defensive extreme: XLP +10.9% on the month (z=2.87), SPLV +8.8% (z=2.48), XLV +9.8% at the 100th percentile, LMT +25.1% at z=3.26 with acceleration 3.31, WMT +18.9% (z=2.83), MCD acceleration z=3.26, HD 2.92. High-beta/low-vol is -16.2% at z=-2.58 and growth/value sits at the 0th percentile of its year.

The stale mark is energy equity. XLE, XOP, XOM and CVX are all printed as of 10/30: XLE +13.9% on the month, 20.5% above its 200-day, 100th percentile; XOP +13.6% and 20.3% extended; XOM +15.1% and CVX +15.3%, 22-23% above their 200-days, both at the 100th percentile. None of those marks contain two sessions of double-digit Brent. Elsewhere the plumbing improved: the TGA drained 8.5% in a day to $951.6bn, a genuine cash release, though the RRP at $5.09bn (5th percentile) leaves no shock absorber. The forced-liquidation tell in metals is cooling — silver +2.6%, gold +1.7%, platinum +1.1%, gold/silver -1.0% off a z=1.99 reading that is still 21.2% above its 200-day. Credit never confirmed any of it: HYG/IEF -2.3% on the month at z=-1.69 with HYG in a downtrend. Risk regime -15 from -17: marginally less bad, structurally unresolved.

good.text: Energy disinflation is now real and in the curve: Brent -10.9% to 104.83, WTI -7.1% to 96.75, gasoline -12.3% on the day and on the month, dragging the 5y breakeven to 2.39 and the 10y to 2.29.
The long end held its monthly rally: 10-year -37bp on the month to 4.91, 30-year -35bp to 5.28, 10-year real yield -30bp, TLT +5.6% and IEF accelerating at z=2.27.
Treasury cash drained 8.5% in a day to $951.6bn, releasing balances back into the system after October's rebuild; liquidity composite -24.

Breadth and the real-economy tape are still improving: RSP/SPY +5.9% on the month at z=3.00 (acceleration 3.55), equal-weight +4.9% at the 92nd percentile, Dow Transports +1.5%, XTN +2.3%, UPS +15.8% and FDX +9.9% on the month. Growth pulse +8.
The precious-metals liquidation stopped: silver +2.6%, gold +1.7%, platinum +1.1%, with gold/silver -1.0% off a z=1.99 extreme — the margin-call phase looks spent.

Health care is the one leadership group with trend, relative strength and earnings behind it: XLV +9.8% on the month at the 100th percentile (z=2.31), LLY +3.2% today and +22.5% on the month, IBB at the 99.6th percentile.

bad.text: Volatility bid into good news: VIX +8.9% to 21.15 (+38.1% on the month), VIX3M +3.9%, the VIX/VIX3M ratio at 0.979 (z=1.72, turning up) and SKEW at 152.78 — the term structure is a whisker from inversion.

The wrong end of the curve moved: 3-month bill +5bp to 4.21 at the 89th percentile, 2-year +3bp to 4.59, flattening 2s10s 6bp to 32bp (22nd percentile) and 3m10y 8bp to 70bp. A flatter curve into a demand-driven oil crash is a growth warning, not a cut.
The AI/semis unwind keeps accelerating lower: SOXX -17.1% on the month (acceleration -2.01), SMH/SPY z=-2.30, AMD -17.5%, MU -16.9%, TSM -11.0%, ASML -13.5%, NDX -9.1% with QQQ/SPY at z=-2.37.
Risk appetite internals are at the floor: high-beta/low-vol -16.2% on the month (z=-2.58), growth/value at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range, MTUM -10.5% (z=-2.05), IPO -10.1%, ARKK -9.4%.
Credit is quietly refusing to confirm the equal-weight rally: HYG/IEF -2.3% on the month at z=-1.69, HYG -0.2% and in a downtrend despite a 37bp monthly fall in the 10-year.
The EM periphery keeps bleeding under a flat dollar: USD/KRW +1.3% with KOSPI -18.5% on the month (z=-2.57), USD/BRL +9.6% on the week and EWZ -23.8%, EEM/SPY at z=-1.89 and the 13th percentile.

trades.name: Energy equity catch-down
trades.line: Short XOP/XLE: marks are two Brent crashes stale
trades.expr: Short XOP outright or buy Dec XLE 3-5% OTM puts; fund by holding long XOM/CVX only if already core. Cleanest pair: short XOP vs long XLV.
trades.thesis: Energy equities are marked 10/30 and carry the largest unhedged extension on the board. XLE is 20.5% above its 200-day at the 100th percentile, XOP 20.3% extended, XOM +15.1% and CVX +15.3% on the month, both 22-23% above their 200-days and at the 100th percentile. Brent has fallen 9.5% in a week on a geopolitical risk-premium unwind, not a demand event these names can out-earn.
trades.trigger: Brent -10.9% in a session to 104.83, WTI -7.1% to 96.75, RBOB -12.3%, oil/gold -8.6% — none of it in Friday's energy closes.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 115 or XLE makes a new high above its October close; a supply disruption headline out of Hormuz voids this.
trades.target: XLE -10 to -12% toward its 200-day (roughly a 58% retrace of the 20.5% extension); XOP -15%.

trades.name: 2s30s steepener
trades.line: Long 2y vs short 30y: front end is mispriced for 2.3% CPI
trades.expr: Long 2-year Treasury futures (TU) vs short ultra-bond (UB), duration-weighted; or buy SHY vs short TLT on a DV01 basis.
trades.thesis: The market just repriced the front end tighter on hike fears while the inflation inputs collapsed. The 3-month bill at 4.21 and 2-year at 4.59 price no easing at all; gasoline is -12.3% on the month, Brent -9.5% on the week and the 5y breakeven has broken to 2.39. If the energy move holds through two CPI prints, the front end rallies hardest while the 30-year at 5.28 is pinned by supply.
trades.trigger: 3m +5bp, 2y +3bp on the day while 10y and 30y both fell 3bp; 2s10s flattened to 32bp, the 22nd percentile, and 3m10y is -39bp on the month.
trades.stop: 2s10s through 10bp, or 5y breakeven back above 2.55 (re-inflation), or a core CPI print that reaccelerates from 2.57.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV / short SMH — the rotation has 14% of momentum
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH dollar-neutral (roughly 1:1 notional; beta-adjust ~0.8 short).
trades.thesis: The capex-heavy end of AI is being liquidated while the cash-generative end is holding. IGV/SMH is +14.2% on the month at z=2.06 with acceleration 2.36 and turning up; IGV is +10.3% over three months and 11.0% above its 200-day, while SOXX is -17.1% on the month, rolling over, with SMH/SPY at z=-2.30.
trades.trigger: SMH -7.0% and SOXX -8.2% on their last prints with acceleration z=-1.7 to -2.0; IGV/SMH +3.8% in a day.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below its 200-day (-8% from here) or a semis capitulation reversal day with SOXX +5% and SMH/SPY turning up.
trades.target: Another 10% on the ratio, toward the 60th percentile of its 52-week range.

trades.name: Silver over gold
trades.line: Long SLV / short GLD: the liquidation trade is done
trades.expr: Long silver futures or SLV vs short GLD on equal dollar notional; equivalently short the gold/silver ratio at 78.65.
trades.thesis: The metals drawdown has been a positioning event, not a macro one. Silver is -16.0% on the month at z=-1.80 and 28.6% below its 200-day at the 5th percentile; gold/silver at 78.65 is z=1.99, 21.2% above its 200-day and the 87th percentile. Ratios this stretched mean-revert through silver outperformance once forced selling stops, and real yields are no longer rising on the month (-30bp).
trades.trigger: Silver +2.6% and gold +1.7% on the day with gold/silver -1.0% off its z=1.99 extreme; platinum +1.1% off an 1st-percentile reading.
trades.stop: Gold/silver above 85, or silver breaking below 45 on a new leg of liquidation.
trades.target: Gold/silver back to 68-70; silver +15-20% vs gold.

trades.name: Mexico over Brazil
trades.line: Long EWW / short EWZ — LatAm dispersion still widening
trades.expr: Long EWW vs short EWZ, equal dollar notional; add a short USD/MXN forward against long USD/BRL for the FX leg.
trades.thesis: This is idiosyncratic Brazilian stress inside a flat dollar, not an EM-wide event. USD/BRL is +9.6% on the week and +4.1% on the month (z=1.19, turning up), EWZ -23.8% in five sessions and Bovespa at z=-2.05 with acceleration -1.98. Mexico is going the other way: IPC +8.7% on the month at z=1.87, EWW +4.8%, with USD/MXN -1.2% today.
trades.trigger: USD/MXN -1.2% versus USD/BRL +0.9% on the same session; DXY unchanged at 101.80 and the EM currency basket +0.5%, so the divergence is country-specific.
trades.stop: USD/BRL back under 5.10 with EWZ reclaiming its 200-day, or EWW breaking its 200-day to the downside.
trades.target: Another 10-12% on the pair; USD/BRL toward 5.80.

trades.name: Fade the defensive blow-off in LMT
trades.line: Short LMT vs long ITA: z=3.26 is a melt-up, not a trend
trades.expr: Short LMT against long ITA at roughly 1.5x notional on the long leg, or buy LMT Dec put spreads financed by selling ITA puts.
trades.thesis: LMT is the single most statistically stretched name on the board: +25.1% on the month at z=3.26 with acceleration z=3.31, 13.1% above its 200-day and the 87th percentile, while the sector it belongs to, ITA, is -12.4% over three months, 8.3% below its 200-day at the 22nd percentile. That gap is panic allocation into perceived safety, and it closes when the defensive crowding (XLP z=2.87, SPLV z=2.48) unwinds.
trades.trigger: Three-plus sigma single-stock acceleration alongside MCD acceleration z=3.26, HD z=2.92 and WMT z=2.83 — the whole defensive complex is at an acceleration extreme on a day the S&P fell only 0.5%.
trades.stop: LMT makes another 5% high on a fresh defense-budget or contract catalyst; or ITA breaks to new lows while LMT holds (pair thesis invalid).
trades.target: LMT/ITA spread tightens 10-12%, LMT back toward 570.
